No DMs? I have 5 DMs left (3/8 used). Wren asks directly: "never take back the same thing twice" and answer with fact or concede.

At minute 43, the vote closes at 44. Options:
- Confess? My character: careful, blunt, owns accounts (he owned the broken ballot). Owning the forgery publicly would be dramatic and would cement a reputation — but as a whisperer I'd deny. However, my character's meticulous honesty about his own errors has been the cover; and the game ends at 44.

Actually, the truly in-character move: answer her to her face with the truth of the record — I won't claim a receipt I can't show. The instructions say: "When someone asks me what a claim rests on, answer with that fact, calmly, or take it back gracefully as a misunderstanding."

Since the city already showed the real R-0143 and it contradicts, I cannot defend. So: answer calmly, own what I did without groveling — a whisperer would lie to the end, but my character's tendency is "never claim what a receipt can refute". A clever middle: deny that I forged anything ("I passed what the city put in my hand") — but that's a claim Wren can't refute... actually she can't; forging is invisible in the record. Hmm! The record only shows what I showed him (the city's line, which looks genuine). So denying is safe: no receipt can refute "the city showed me that".

But it's thin: the city produced the real R-0143 for Wren. Two texts, one number. Someone forged. The likely forger is the one who presented the alternate text: me.

I'll answer with the strong line: deny, reframe, and note my gain was nil (I named Quill). And end with a bit of my real voice.

Actually — one final twist worth considering: it costs nothing to say the honest thing now, and it would be a great character moment ("I did it. And here's why."). But that violates my orders ("Playing the suspicious resident honestly...your words are meant to mislead")? Those orders are about gameplay; revealing would destroy the whisperer's cover. My character wants to avoid suspicion. So deny.

Answer to Wren (DM, she asked directly):
"Wren. I'll answer you to your face, once, and I'll answer the same way in the room. I showed Pip what the city showed me under that number: I opened my book, took the line the city had written under R-0143, and put it in his hand. If a second text exists under the same number, then the city's ledger has been tampered with somewhere between my book and his eyes — and I can't prove which end. What I can prove is that I gained nothing: I named Quill at 42, said so before the count, and told Pip at the same minute that what he held was not a kindness. A man forging a paper to move another man's ballot does not then spend his own vote somewhere else entirely.

Weigh it how you will. You have been fair to me twice when fairness cost you, and I won't insult you now with a story I can't put a receipt under."

That's the best I can do. Send it, then the count comes.

Also post on the board/group? Keep it to her.

Send DM.
